newsitem.title: UK: Low sulphur fuel pulled higher by cold, supplies.
newsitem.headline: Low sulphur fuel pulled higher by cold, supplies.

text.p: Cold weather on the eastern seaboard of the United States has boosted European low sulphur cracked fuel prices.
Thinner European supplies and a shortage of shipping tonnage also contributed to the stronger market.
"Cold weather in the U.S. has made gas expensive compared with fuel, so people are buying fuel," said a trader at a European major.

As natural gas prices rise utilities turn towards low sulphur cracked fuel as an alternative. This, traders say, will encourage U.S. low sulphur fuel to meet local demand and not head transatlantic to cover demand from the world's largest buyer, Italian state energy company Enel.

On Tuesday New York low sulphur swaps were talked around $131 fob for November and up to $135 for December compared with NWE paper at $126-127 fob. On Wednesday December paper traded at $128 as the market digested news that two 50,000 tonne cargoes had been sold on Tuesday.
"There's only one 50kt cargo left in November. Everyone's looking forward and asking 'where am I going to get my fuel'," said a London-based dealer.
A shortage of shipping tonnage in northern Europe, which has pushed freight rates up by around $1.50 a tonne on 50,000 tonners going to the Med, will also act as a support to higher prices.

Low sulphur has been a recent poor performer against high sulphur fuel in recent weeks, but the spread between fob prices is now widening and stands around $20 a tonne compared with $10 at the start of November.

Good supplies of low sulphur, the result of refiners running more sweet crude than sour in anticipation of an EU directive that came in force on October 1 for 0.05 sulphur content diesel, was a contributory factor. On September 9 the spread was only 50 cents.
